newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt wants 97 native title solution.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt wants 97 native title solution.

text.p: The Australian government said on Friday it will have to find a solution this year to a controversial High Court ruling that has raised land ownership problems between pastoral lease holders and native Aboriginals.
"The government has said there is no timetable but my opinion is we have to find a solution this year," Senator Nick Minchin, parliamentary secretary to Prime Minister John Howard, said.
Minchin was speaking after a keynote address to a conference discussing his conservative Liberal-National Party government's considerations of a response to the High Court ruling.
The position of pastoral leases has been thrown into doubt by the recent High Court ruling that pastoral leases do not automatically over-ride Aboriginal native title.

The High Court in a split decision, made its ruling on a claim by two Aboriginal groups, the Wik and Thayorre tribes, against an earlier lower court ruling that pastoral leases extinguished native title.
Howard's coalition government has said it will convene top-level talks to try to find a solution.
About 40 percent of Australia's land area is under pastoral leases, including many mining and exploration permit areas.

The preamble to the Native Title Act passed by the former Labor government into law in 1994 said it was intended that pastoral leases should extinguish native title but this was not incorporated in the act.
Farmers and miners say the court's decision has thrown a pall of uncertainty over their ability to do anything on leasehold land.
Minchin said the government would observe the basic principles of the Racial Discrimination Act in its attempts to find a solution.
"But we have said all options are open, except doing nothing or overturning the original legislation," Minchin said.
Earlier, native title negotiator, Noel Pearson told reporters that Aboriginal groups would not participate in talks that resulted in any changes to the Racial Discrimination Act.
"I am concerned that the opportunity to find solutions is not lost," Pearson said.
Earlier in Friday, the junior partner in Australia's coalition government, the rural-based National Party, urged the government to legislate to guarantee pastoral leases against native land claims.
A legislative solution to quash native title on pastoral land has been urged by pastoralists and state governments, but rejected by Aboriginal groups who favour regional negotiations.
People of Aboriginal descent make up less than two percent of Australia's 18 million population.
